steps.question: Which color roles does it need?
steps.why: Few color roles, each with one clear meaning.
Shadows are hard to see; borders are not.

steps.pick: neutral.0: the base for content; body text reads 18.42:1 on it, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: We use the step above the page for content in dark in order to leave a darker step free for wells, as the gray's two darkest steps are too close to tell apart. The fill does this by moving content one step up: sunken reads 1.16:1 below it and raised 1.26:1 above it. So people tell wells and menus from content, and body text still reads 14.85:1, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), text keeps the AAA floor (accessibility.definition) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.36:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.300: We use the step above the raised surface for dividers and card borders in dark in order to give separation on every surface a line meets, menus included. The line does this by staying lighter than each surface, lowest 1.8:1, on surface.raised. So rows and cards stay apart on content and in menus, because lines separate groups (elevation.definition) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

steps.pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. The largest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 6px controls inside it. So a step card reads as one object that holds its fields, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is calm and clear (brand.q1).

steps.question: How big are icons next to text?
steps.why: Larger icons are easier to see.

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?

steps.use: Badge with an icon and a word
steps.why: Status must survive no color and a screen reader.

steps.pick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 18.42:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 14.85:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?
Where do the words matter most?
steps.why: Words decide whether a form gets finished.
Large text and short lines lower effort.

steps.pick: neutral.500: the quietest text that still reads, 7.0:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.600: We use the quietest readable gray for hints and captions in dark in order to keep muted text a step below secondary text (neutral.700). The step does this by reading 7.67:1 on surface.default and 6.09:1 on surface.raised, the lightest surface it meets. Raised layers fall under 7:1 by the owner's recorded exception for muted text, the one light mode takes too, as the next gray up is secondary's own step. So people read a hint in a menu as well as on the page, because text keeps the AAA floor (accessibility.definition) and the neutral ramp has no step between muted and secondary (color.definition).

steps.question: Which color roles does it need?
steps.why: Few color roles, each with one clear meaning.

steps.question: What is a costly mistake?
steps.why: A failed form can cost someone a benefit.

steps.use: color.status.danger, an icon and a sentence next to the field
steps.why: People must know what went wrong and where.

steps.use: Say what is wrong, where, and exactly how to fix it
steps.why: People must be able to fix the error without help.

steps.rule: Real risk: errors, failed checks, actions that cannot be undone. The top of the urgency order. Overuse wears it out.
steps.pick: red.light.700: danger reads as text and icons, 8.55:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: red.dark.900: We use the palest red but one for danger in dark in order to keep error labels at 7:1 in alerts on content and in destructive menu items, and apart from info for every eye. The step does this by reading 12.39:1 on surface.default and 9.84:1 on surface.raised. Below it, the key (red.dark.600) gives 5.32:1 and red.dark.700 6.8:1 on the raised layer, and red.dark.800 sits within 0.02 of status.info under protanopia. The danger button keeps the key as its fill, and danger text on dark fills is as pale already. So people read an error or a destructive action at full strength in every layer, because text keeps the AAA floor (accessibility.definition) and danger lands in alerts and menus (color.lands).
